Product UX · Tablet ordering

Rose Family Bakery POS

Taking a custom cake order is a conversation. I designed a tablet workflow that lets staff keep track of the details while they talk with the customer.

Design focus Turn bakery rules into a workflow staff can follow during a conversation.

PROJECT CONTEXT

Project and approach

At the counter, someone has to confirm the date, pick the cake options, get the message right, and explain the price. I used low- and mid-fidelity wireframes to work out when staff need each piece of information and what they should be able to see as the order takes shape.

01 / DESIGN DECISIONS

Check the date before customizing the cake

The bakery brief calls for at least 48 hours’ notice and allows orders up to 60 days ahead. I put scheduling before product selection so staff can confirm the pickup date before spending time talking through flavors, sizes, and decorations.

02 / DESIGN DECISIONS

Keep the running order in view

While staff enter size, flavor, theme, quantity, and a message of up to 50 characters, the current order stays beside the options. If a customer asks what they’ve already chosen, staff can check the summary without leaving the screen.

03 / DESIGN DECISIONS

Give staff a chance to catch mistakes

I gave order review its own step before payment. Staff can read the details back to the customer, change or remove an item, and explain the subtotal, delivery charge, and total while there’s still time to make a correction.

REFLECTION

What I learned and what I’d test next

The wireframes show how the scheduling rules, running order, and review step fit together. I’d test the flow with bakery staff using an order that needs a changed cake option and an earlier pickup date. I’d watch whether they spot the timing issue and can correct the order without losing the details they already entered.
